children.title: Intangible Assets Not Subject to Amortization
children.summary: This section discusses intangible assets not subject to amortization, specifically focusing on wireless licenses that grant exclusive rights to utilize radio frequency spectrum for communication services. These licenses are treated as indefinite-lived assets due to their routine renewals and lack of limiting factors affecting their useful life. The section outlines the annual impairment testing process for these licenses, including qualitative and quantitative assessments, and describes the Greenfield approach used to estimate their fair value. Additionally, it mentions the capitalization of interest expenses related to preparing the licenses for use and the accounting treatment of auction deposits for acquiring new licenses.

children.title: Intangible Assets Subject to Amortization and Long-Lived Assets
children.summary: This section discusses the treatment of intangible assets subject to amortization and long-lived assets, specifically focusing on customer lists and non-network internal-use software, which are amortized over their useful lives. It outlines the process for reviewing these assets for impairment, which involves comparing the carrying amount to expected net undiscounted cash flows. If impairment indicators are present, a fair value assessment is conducted to determine if an impairment charge is necessary. Additionally, the section emphasizes the annual re-evaluation of useful life determinations for these intangible assets.

children.title: Leases
children.summary: This section discusses the leasing practices of the company, detailing the types of leases (operating and finance) for network equipment and real estate. It explains the assessment process for determining lease classification and the initial measurement of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at lease commencement. The section also covers the calculation of present value for lease payments using incremental borrowing rates, the treatment of non-lease components, and the recognition of rent expenses. Additionally, it outlines the accounting for short-term leases and the amortization of right-of-use assets for finance leases, including the recognition of interest expenses.

children.title: Fair Value Measurements
children.summary: This section defines fair value measurements for financial and non-financial assets and liabilities as an exit price in orderly transactions. It outlines a three-tier hierarchy for inputs used in fair value measurement: Level 1 (quoted prices in active markets), Level 2 (observable inputs), and Level 3 (unobservable inputs). The classification of financial assets and liabilities is based on the lowest level of significant input, which requires management judgment and can impact valuation. Readers can learn about the importance of input significance in fair value assessments and the implications for financial reporting.

children.title: Income Taxes
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's effective tax rate, which is influenced by pre-tax income, statutory tax rates, and applicable tax laws and regulations. It explains the concept of deferred income taxes, which arise from temporary differences between financial statement and income tax assets and liabilities. The section also details the annual recalculation of deferred income taxes at the applicable tax rates and the use of valuation allowances to ensure deferred tax assets are realizable. Readers can learn about the tax planning strategies employed by Verizon and how they impact financial reporting.

children.title: Stock-Based Compensation
children.summary: This section discusses the measurement and recognition of stock-based compensation expenses for employees and directors, which are based on estimated fair values. It emphasizes the importance of fair value estimation in accounting for stock-based awards and refers readers to Note 10 for further details. The section highlights the impact of stock-based compensation on financial statements and the need for management judgment in these evaluations.

children.title: Foreign Currency Translation and Transactions
children.summary: This section outlines the foreign currency translation and transaction processes for the company's foreign operations, which typically use the local currency as their functional currency. Financial statements of these foreign entities are translated into U.S. dollars using average exchange rates for income statement items and end-of-period rates for assets and liabilities. Translation adjustments are recorded in Accumulated other comprehensive loss within equity, while exchange gains and losses from currency conversions are included in Other income (expense), net. This approach helps in accurately reflecting the financial position and performance of foreign operations in the consolidated financial statements.

children.title: Employee Benefit Plans
children.summary: This section outlines the accounting treatment for employee benefit plans, including pension and postretirement health care and life insurance benefits. It details how benefits are accrued, the amortization of prior service costs, and the recognition of actuarial gains and losses. The funded status of pension and postretirement plans is recognized as an asset or liability on the balance sheet, and unrecognized prior service costs are included in accumulated other comprehensive income. Additionally, it notes that Verizon management employees no longer earn pension benefits or service towards retiree medical subsidies.

children.title: Derivative Instruments
children.summary: This section discusses the use of derivative instruments by the company to manage exposure to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. It details the types of derivatives employed, such as cross currency swaps and interest rate caps, and clarifies that these instruments are not held for trading purposes. The section explains the measurement of derivatives at fair value, their classification as assets or liabilities, and the accounting treatment for changes in their fair value, including the impact on earnings and other comprehensive income. Additionally, it outlines the cash flow presentation of derivatives in relation to hedged items.

children.title: Variable Interest Entities
children.summary: This section discusses Variable Interest Entities (VIEs), which are entities that do not have enough equity to independently finance their activities and rely on additional financial support from other parties. It explains the characteristics of VIEs, including the lack of decision-making power among equity investors. The section likely outlines the accounting treatment and implications for financial reporting related to VIEs, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and measuring the financial interests in such entities. Readers can learn about the criteria that define VIEs and the potential impact on a company's financial statements.

children.title: Recently Adopted Accounting Standards
children.summary: This section discusses the adoption of ASU 2016-13, which pertains to Financial Instruments - Credit Losses, effective January 1, 2020. It details the cumulative after-tax effect on retained earnings, showing a reduction of $200 million. The section also references additional disclosures related to credit losses and outlines revenue generation from contracts with customers, categorized by Consumer and Business segments. It highlights the treatment of month-to-month service contracts and the allocation of transaction prices to performance obligations, emphasizing the practical expedient under Topic 606 for contracts with a duration of one year or less.

children.title: Note 2. Revenue and Contract Costs
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's revenue recognition and contract costs, detailing revenue by category for Consumer and Business segments, including additional sources like leasing and insurance. It explains Remaining Performance Obligations (RPOs) under Topic 606, focusing on unsatisfied obligations and the practical expedient for short-term contracts. The section also distinguishes between accounts receivable and contract balances, providing key figures and discussing the impact of sales promotions. Lastly, it addresses the accounting treatment of contract costs, including the deferral and amortization of costs incurred to obtain contracts, with financial data for contract assets and liabilities.

children.title: Revenue by Category
children.summary: This section details the revenue generated by the company, categorized into two main segments: Consumer and Business. It explains how revenue is disaggregated by products and services for the Consumer segment and by customer groups for the Business segment. The section also discusses additional revenue sources not accounted for under Topic 606, such as leasing arrangements and insurance revenues. Furthermore, it highlights the concept of remaining performance obligations, particularly focusing on month-to-month service contracts and their impact on revenue recognition.

children.title: Remaining Performance Obligations
children.summary: This section discusses the concept of Remaining Performance Obligations (RPOs) in relation to revenue recognition under Topic 606. It explains how the total contract transaction price is allocated to performance obligations, particularly focusing on unsatisfied or partially satisfied obligations at the end of the reporting period. The section highlights the practical expedient that allows exclusion of expected revenues from contracts with an original duration of one year or less, noting that a significant portion of contracts are month-to-month. It also details the nature of various service contracts, including their terms and conditions, and the implications for revenue recognition.

children.title: Accounts Receivable and Contract Balances
children.summary: This section discusses the timing and recognition of revenue related to accounts receivable and contract balances at Verizon. It explains the distinction between receivables, which represent an unconditional right to payment, and contract balances, which include contract assets and liabilities. Key figures include receivables totaling $11.3 billion and contract liabilities of $8.2 billion as of December 31, 2022. The section also details how contract assets arise from the difference between recognized equipment revenue and customer payments, and how contract liabilities increase due to advance billing for services. Additionally, it highlights the impact of sales promotions and contract modifications on these balances.

children.title: Contract Costs
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment of contract costs under Topic 606, emphasizing the recognition and amortization of incremental costs incurred to obtain customer contracts, such as commission expenses. It explains how these costs are deferred and amortized over the expected benefit periods, which vary for wireless and wireline contracts. The section also provides financial data on contract assets and liabilities, including balances for deferred contract costs and related expenses recognized in the financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2022, and 2021. Additionally, it outlines the criteria for deferring costs to fulfill contracts and the assessment of these costs for impairment.

children.title: Note 3. Acquisitions and Divestitures
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's strategic acquisitions and divestitures, including significant spectrum license transactions from FCC auctions, such as Auction 103 and Auction 107, and the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc. for approximately $3.5 billion, enhancing its prepaid services market. It details the acquisition of Bluegrass Cellular for $412 million, aimed at expanding services in rural Kentucky. Additionally, it discusses the divestiture of Verizon Media to Apollo Global Management for $4.3 billion, resulting in a pre-tax gain of $1.0 billion, and outlines the financial implications of these transactions, including cash proceeds, performance-based contingent considerations, and ongoing technical support agreements.

children.title: Spectrum License Transactions
children.summary: This section details Verizon's spectrum license transactions, including significant participation in FCC auctions. In March 2020, Verizon acquired 4,940 licenses in Auction 103 for $3.4 billion, with a pre-tax net loss of $1.2 billion recorded due to the exchange of licenses. In February 2021, Verizon won licenses in Auction 107 for $45.5 billion, with additional estimated payments of $7.7 billion for clearing costs. The section also discusses agreements made in March 2022 for early clearance of C-Band spectrum, costing approximately $340 million, and various other wireless license acquisitions. Additionally, it covers the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc. for approximately $3.5 billion, enhancing Verizon's market position in prepaid services.

children.title: Business Acquisitions and Divestitures
children.summary: This section details Verizon's business acquisitions and divestitures, focusing on significant transactions such as the acquisition of TracFone Wireless, Inc. for approximately $3.5 billion in cash and stock, which enhances Verizon's position in the prepaid mobile services market. It outlines the financial terms of the acquisition, including contingent consideration based on performance metrics, and notes the cash proceeds received from working capital settlements. Additionally, it discusses Verizon's participation in FCC spectrum auctions, including Auction 103 and Auction 107, highlighting the financial implications and future payment obligations associated with these licenses. The section emphasizes the strategic importance of these acquisitions and spectrum transactions for Verizon's growth and network expansion.

children.title: Bluegrass Cellular
children.summary: This section details Verizon's acquisition of Bluegrass Cellular, a rural wireless operator in central Kentucky, which was finalized in March 2021 for approximately $412 million. It outlines the financial aspects of the acquisition, including the cash consideration and the net assets acquired. The section also discusses the implications of the acquisition on Verizon's financial statements, including the allocation of purchase price to various assets and liabilities. Additionally, it highlights the strategic importance of the acquisition in expanding Verizon's service offerings in rural areas.

children.title: Verizon Media Divestiture
children.summary: On May 2, 2021, Verizon agreed to sell Verizon Media to an affiliate of Apollo Global Management for $4.3 billion in cash, along with additional equity interests. The sale was completed on September 1, 2021, resulting in a pre-tax gain of approximately $1.0 billion for Verizon. The section details the financial implications of the sale, including cash proceeds and costs incurred, as well as the ongoing relationship through Transition Services Agreements for technical support. It also notes the revenue generated by Verizon Media in the years prior to the sale and subsequent redemptions of preferred partnership interests by the Apollo Affiliate.

children.title: Other
children.summary: This section details Verizon's divestiture of Verizon Media to Apollo Global Management for $4.3 billion, completed on September 1, 2021, resulting in a pre-tax gain of approximately $1.0 billion. It also discusses the financial implications of the sale, including cash proceeds and the fair value of partnership units. Additionally, it mentions Verizon's ongoing technical support under Transition Services Agreements and provides insights into wireless licenses, including their carrying amounts, capitalized interest, and impairment assessments. The section concludes with information on other acquisitions and divestitures, including a pre-tax gain from a separate investment sale.

children.title: Note 4. Wireless Licenses, Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's wireless licenses, reporting a carrying amount of $149.8 billion as of December 31, 2022, with $41.7 billion under development and no impairment noted for 2021 and 2022. It details changes in Goodwill, highlighting significant amounts from acquisitions like TracFone and an impairment charge for an early-stage company, while assessing future impairment risks for the Business unit. Additionally, it outlines the composition and amortization of Other Intangible Assets, including customer lists and software, with historical and estimated future amortization expenses, and notes the impact of asset disposals from the Verizon Media sale and TracFone acquisition.

children.title: Wireless Licenses
children.summary: This section details Verizon's wireless licenses, reporting a carrying amount of $149.8 billion as of December 31, 2022, up from $147.6 billion in 2021. It highlights that approximately $41.7 billion of these licenses were under development, with $1.7 billion in capitalized interest recorded in 2022. The section also notes the renewal of various licenses in compliance with FCC regulations, averaging 15 years for 2022. Additionally, it discusses the annual impairment testing of wireless licenses, indicating no impairment for both 2021 and 2022 based on qualitative and quantitative assessments.

children.title: Goodwill
children.summary: This section details the changes in the carrying amount of Goodwill for the company, including balances at the beginning and end of 2021 and 2022, acquisitions, and adjustments. It highlights significant goodwill related to acquisitions such as TracFone and notes an impairment charge related to an early-stage development company. The section also discusses qualitative and quantitative impairment assessments performed for the Consumer and Business reporting units, indicating that their fair values exceeded carrying values, though there is an increasing risk of future impairment for the Business unit due to potential revenue declines. Additionally, it outlines factors that could negatively impact fair value, including competitive pressures and macroeconomic changes.

children.title: Other Intangible Assets
children.summary: This section details the composition and amortization of Other Intangible Assets as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. It includes specific figures for customer lists, non-network internal-use software, and other intangible assets, along with their respective gross amounts, accumulated amortization, and net amounts. The section also provides historical amortization expenses for the years 2020 to 2022 and estimates future amortization expenses for 2023 to 2027. Additionally, it notes the impact of asset disposals related to the Verizon Media sale and the acquisition of TracFone.

children.title: Note 5. Property, Plant and Equipment
children.summary: This section provides a detailed breakdown of Property, Plant and Equipment (PP&E) as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021, including costs associated with land, buildings, equipment, and other assets. It lists the useful lives of various asset categories, such as central office equipment (3 to 15 years) and antennas (4 to 50 years). The total PP&E is reported at $307,689 million for 2022, with accumulated depreciation of $200,255 million, resulting in a net value of $107,434 million. The section highlights the growth in PP&E from the previous year and provides insights into the company's investment in physical assets.

children.title: Note 6. Leasing Arrangements
children.summary: This section details Verizon's leasing arrangements for network equipment, real estate, and other assets, highlighting lease terms ranging from 1 to 30 years, with options for extensions and terminations. It discusses a significant transaction with American Tower Corporation involving the leasing of 11,300 wireless towers, including the financial implications and responsibilities related to ground leases. The section provides a breakdown of net lease costs, including operating and finance lease expenses, and outlines cash flow disclosures related to these leases. Additionally, it presents the weighted-average remaining lease terms and discount rates for operating and finance leases, along with a maturity analysis of lease liabilities as of December 31, 2022.

children.title: Note 7. Debt
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive overview of Verizon's debt activities for the year ended December 31, 2022, detailing significant debt transactions, short-term borrowing, asset-backed debt, and long-term credit facilities. It highlights $5,032 million in notes purchased, $2,093 million in principal repaid, and the issuance of $1 billion in new notes. The section also discusses the company's asset-backed debt totaling $20 billion, including ABS Notes and financing facilities, as well as non-cash transactions and net debt extinguishment losses. Additionally, it covers guarantees on debentures for subsidiaries and compliance with debt covenants, indicating the company's financial stability and management of debt obligations.

children.title: 2022 Significant Debt Transactions
children.summary: The section covers Verizon's significant debt transactions for the year ended December 31, 2022, including tender offers, repayments, redemptions, and new issuances. It details a total of $5,032 million in notes purchased, $2,093 million in principal repaid or repurchased, and the issuance of new notes such as $1 billion in 3.875% notes due 2052. Additionally, it highlights $18.9 billion in total repayments and the issuance of green bonds for renewable energy projects. The section also discusses short-term borrowing activities, including a $1 billion credit facility and $27.4 billion in commercial paper, with a carrying value of asset-backed debt at $20 billion as of year-end.

children.title: Tender Offers
children.summary: This section details Verizon's tender offers and significant debt transactions for the year ended December 31, 2022. It outlines the principal amounts purchased and cash considerations for various notes and debentures, including a total of $5,032 million in Verizon notes due 2032-2056. Additionally, it provides information on repayments, redemptions, and repurchases, highlighting a total of $2,093 million in principal repaid or repurchased. The section also mentions the issuance of new notes, including $1,000 million in 3.875% notes due 2052, with net proceeds used for renewable energy projects. Overall, it emphasizes Verizon's financial strategies to manage debt and maintain capital structure.

children.title: Repayments, Redemptions and Repurchases
children.summary: This section details Verizon's financial activities related to repayments, redemptions, and repurchases of long-term borrowings, totaling $18.9 billion, including $4.8 billion for asset-backed borrowings. It outlines significant debt transactions for 2022, including tender offers and open market repurchases, with a total of $2.1 billion repaid or repurchased. The section also highlights the issuance of new notes, including green bonds aimed at funding renewable energy projects, and discusses short-term borrowing activities, including a $1.0 billion credit facility and commercial paper transactions. Additionally, it provides information on the carrying value of asset-backed debt as of December 31, 2022.

children.title: Issuances
children.summary: This section details Verizon's significant debt issuances and transactions for the year ended December 31, 2022. It highlights the issuance of various notes, including $1 billion in 3.875% notes due 2052 and €1.25 billion in 4.250% notes due 2030, with total net proceeds amounting to $4.09 billion. The section also discusses the company's short-term borrowing activities, including a $1 billion credit facility and $27.4 billion in commercial paper issued, with $150 million outstanding at year-end. Additionally, it mentions the carrying value of asset-backed debt, which stood at $20 billion as of December 31, 2022, and includes details on the types of asset-backed debt involved.

children.title: Short-term Borrowing and Commercial Paper Program
children.summary: In 2022, Verizon utilized a $1.0 billion short-term uncommitted credit facility, which was fully drawn and repaid by December 31, 2022, leaving no short-term borrowings outstanding. The company issued $27.4 billion in commercial paper and repaid $27.3 billion, resulting in $150 million of commercial paper remaining at year-end. Additionally, as of December 31, 2022, Verizon's asset-backed debt totaled $20.0 billion, comprising Asset-Backed Notes and loans from banks. These financial activities are detailed in the consolidated statements of cash flows, highlighting Verizon's management of short-term financing and debt obligations.

children.title: Asset-Backed Debt
children.summary: As of December 31, 2022, Verizon's asset-backed debt totaled $20.0 billion, comprising Asset-Backed Notes (ABS Notes) and loans from banks. The debt is secured by receivables from device payment plans and other agreements, which are transferred to bankruptcy-remote entities (ABS Entities) that issue the debt. Verizon retains equity interests in these entities, which entitle it to funds not needed for debt payments. Investors and banks have recourse only to the collateralized assets, not to Verizon itself. Cash collections on these receivables are deposited into segregated accounts, classified as restricted cash in financial statements.

children.title: ABS Notes
children.summary: This section details the transactions related to Asset-Backed Securities (ABS) Notes for the year ending December 31, 2022. It includes specific data on various series of notes issued, including principal amounts, interest rates, and weighted-average life to maturity. The total principal amount issued for the year was $4.485 billion, with a breakdown of transactions occurring in January, May, August, and November. Additionally, it outlines the repayment of $4.3 billion on ABS Notes that entered the amortization period, compared to $3.3 billion in the previous year, highlighting the company's financial activities and obligations related to ABS Notes.

children.title: ABS Financing Facilities
children.summary: This section details the ABS Financing Facilities, including the issuance of $932 million in ABS Notes in January 2023 at a 4.511% interest rate. It outlines the transactions under the 2021 ABS Financing Facility, including prepayments and borrowings totaling $7.9 billion as of December 31, 2022. Additionally, it describes the 2022 ABS Financing Facility, which involves $2.0 billion in asset-backed loans secured by wireless service accounts receivables, with a maturity date in June 2024. The section also explains the classification of ABS Entities as Variable Interest Entities (VIEs), which are consolidated in the financial results, detailing related assets and liabilities as of December 31, 2022.

children.title: Variable Interest Entities
children.summary: This section discusses the issuance of $932 million in ABS Notes in January 2023 and details the ABS Financing Facilities, including significant transactions from 2021 to 2022. It outlines the 2021 ABS Financing Facility, which had an outstanding balance of $7.9 billion as of December 31, 2022, and the 2022 ABS Financing Facility, which involved $2.0 billion in borrowings. The section explains that the ABS Entities qualify as Variable Interest Entities (VIEs), with the company as the primary beneficiary, leading to the consolidation of their assets and liabilities in the financial results. Specific asset and liability figures as of December 31, 2022, are provided, highlighting accounts receivable, prepaid expenses, and long-term debt.

children.title: Long-Term Credit Facilities
children.summary: This section details Verizon's long-term credit facilities as of December 31, 2022, including a $9.5 billion revolving credit facility and various export credit facilities totaling $11 billion. The revolving credit facility allows borrowing without financial covenants and has not been drawn upon since inception. It also discusses the company's borrowing history, including $3 billion drawn in 2022 from export credit facilities, and outlines non-cash transactions related to financing long-lived assets. Additionally, it covers net debt extinguishment losses recorded over the past three years and guarantees on debentures for subsidiaries, along with compliance with debt covenants.

children.title: Non-Cash Transactions
children.summary: This section details non-cash transactions related to financing arrangements for long-lived assets, primarily network equipment, amounting to $832 million, $461 million, and $1.7 billion for the years 2022, 2021, and 2020, respectively. It highlights that these transactions are not included in capital expenditures in cash flow statements. Additionally, it discusses net debt extinguishment losses recorded over the same years, totaling $1.1 billion in 2022, and guarantees on debentures of operating subsidiaries, with $614 million outstanding as of December 31, 2022. The section also confirms compliance with debt covenants and provides a breakdown of accounts receivable, including device payment plans and wireless service receivables.

children.title: Net Debt Extinguishment Losses
children.summary: This section details the net debt extinguishment losses recorded by the company for the years ending December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020, amounting to $1.1 billion, $3.6 billion, and $121 million, respectively. These losses are categorized under Other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of income and affect cash flow from operating and financing activities. The section emphasizes the financial impact of debt extinguishment on the company's overall financial health and reporting.

children.title: Guarantees
children.summary: This section details the guarantees provided by the company for the debentures of its operating telephone company subsidiaries, with an outstanding aggregate principal amount of $614 million as of December 31, 2022. It specifies that these guarantees remain effective for the life of the obligation unless terminated under certain conditions, such as the subsidiary no longer being wholly-owned. Additionally, it confirms compliance with all restrictive covenants in debt agreements, indicating the company's financial stability and adherence to contractual obligations.

children.title: Debt Covenants
children.summary: This section details Verizon's compliance with restrictive covenants in its debt agreements, indicating that both the company and its consolidated subsidiaries are adhering to these financial obligations. It also provides an overview of long-term credit facilities, including a $9.5 billion revolving credit facility that does not impose financial covenants and various export credit facilities with a total capacity of $11 billion. Additionally, it mentions non-cash transactions related to financing long-lived assets and outlines net debt extinguishment losses over the past three years. Lastly, it discusses guarantees related to debentures of operating subsidiaries, with $614 million outstanding as of December 31, 2022.

children.title: Note 8. Device Payment Plan Agreement and Wireless Service Receivables
children.summary: This section covers the financial management and reporting of Verizon's wireless device payment plan agreement receivables, totaling $16.0 billion as of December 31, 2021. It details the structure of the payment program, promotional trade-in agreements, and customer credit risk assessment processes, emphasizing the impact of customer tenure on payment reliability. The section also discusses the origination of device payment plan agreements, credit quality assessment for both Consumer and Business customers, and the methodology for calculating expected credit losses. Additionally, it outlines the allowance for credit losses related to these agreements, including provisions, write-offs, and recoveries for the year ending December 31, 2022.

children.title: Wireless Device Payment Plan Agreement Receivables
children.summary: This section details the financial reporting and management of wireless device payment plan agreement receivables, totaling $16.0 billion as of December 31, 2021. It explains the structure of the Verizon device payment program, where eligible customers can purchase devices with lower service fees compared to fixed-term plans. The section includes a breakdown of receivables, including gross amounts, unamortized interest, and allowances, as well as the accounting for promotional trade-in agreements and customer credits. Additionally, it discusses the credit risk assessment process for customers entering device payment agreements, emphasizing the predictive value of customer tenure on payment reliability.

children.title: Promotions
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's promotions related to device payment plan agreements, including upgrade options for customers who meet specific payment criteria and trade-in conditions. It details the accounting treatment for trade-in rights, including the recognition of a guarantee obligation and the fair value measurement of these liabilities, which were $54 million in 2022 and $77 million in 2021. Additionally, it outlines the trade-in liability, which increased from $366 million in 2021 to $562 million in 2022, and mentions future billing credits as contract liabilities. The section also explains the credit risk assessment process for customers entering device payment plans, emphasizing the predictive value of customer tenure on payment reliability.

children.title: Origination of Device Payment Plan Agreements
children.summary: This section discusses the origination process of device payment plan agreements at Verizon, highlighting the use of internal and external data sources to assess customer credit risk. It explains how customer tenure influences creditworthiness, with longer-tenured customers showing better payment reliability. The section also differentiates between 'established' and 'short-tenured' customers in lending decisions. Additionally, it provides insights into the financial reporting of device payment plan receivables and related liabilities, including trade-in and upgrade promotions.

children.title: Credit Quality Information
children.summary: This section outlines the credit quality assessment processes for both Consumer and Business customers, distinguishing between established and short-tenured customers based on their duration of service. It details how custom credit risk scores are generated using internal and external data to evaluate the likelihood of delinquency. The section also presents data on device payment plan agreement receivables by credit quality indicator as of December 31, 2022, and discusses the methodology for estimating expected credit losses, including the use of proprietary loss models and historical data. Additionally, it explains how the allowance for credit losses is calculated for different customer groups, emphasizing the importance of credit quality indicators in financial assessments.

children.title: Allowance for Credit Losses
children.summary: This section discusses the allowance for credit losses related to device payment plan agreements and wireless service receivables. It outlines the classification of customers as 'established' or 'short-tenured' based on their duration with the company, and how credit risk scores are generated using both internal and external data. The section details the methodology for calculating expected credit losses, including the use of proprietary loss models and historical data. It also provides a summary of the allowance for credit losses activity, including provisions, write-offs, and recoveries for the year ending December 31, 2022, along with the aging of receivables.

children.title: Note 9. Fair Value Measurements and Financial Instruments
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive overview of fair value measurements and financial instruments, focusing on the company's use of recurring fair value measurements for debt and derivative instruments. It details the decline in total fair value from 2021 to 2022 and discusses the use of interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps for risk management, including their accounting treatment and impact on financial statements. Additionally, it covers treasury rate locks and net investment hedges to mitigate interest rate and foreign exchange risks, along with the use of undesignated derivatives as economic hedges. The section also addresses concentrations of credit risk related to financial instruments and the collateral arrangements in place to manage counterparty risk.

children.title: Recurring Fair Value Measurements
children.summary: This section covers the fair value measurements of short-term and long-term debt, employing Level 1 and Level 2 methods based on market prices for similar instruments. It reports a decline in total fair value from $169,205 million in 2021 to $139,041 million in 2022. Additionally, it discusses the company's use of derivative instruments, including interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps, to mitigate risks related to foreign currency and interest rate fluctuations, providing details on notional amounts and pre-tax financial impacts. Tables summarizing the notional values and effects of these derivatives are also included.

children.title: Fair Value of Short-term and Long-term Debt
children.summary: This section details the fair value assessment of short-term and long-term debt, utilizing Level 1 and Level 2 measurement methods based on quoted prices for identical and similar debt instruments. It provides specific fair value figures for the years ending December 31, 2021, and 2022, highlighting a decrease in total fair value from $169,205 million to $139,041 million. Additionally, it discusses the company's use of derivative instruments to manage exposure to foreign currency and interest rate fluctuations, including notional amounts and pre-tax gains or losses associated with various derivatives such as interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps. The section also includes tables summarizing the notional values and financial impacts of these derivatives over the specified years.

children.title: Derivative Instruments
children.summary: The section on Derivative Instruments covers the use of interest rate swaps and cross currency swaps to manage interest rate and foreign currency risks. It details the accounting treatment of these instruments, including their classification as fair value hedges and cash flow hedges, and how changes in their fair value affect interest expense and other comprehensive income. The section also discusses forward starting interest rate swaps for hedging future cash flow variability related to anticipated debt issuances, emphasizing the company's strategies for mitigating interest rate risk and the financial reporting implications of these derivatives.

children.title: Interest Rate Swaps
children.summary: This section discusses the use of interest rate swaps to manage the mix of fixed and variable rate debt, primarily receiving fixed rates and paying variable rates, which affects interest expense. It details the accounting treatment of these swaps as fair value hedges, including their recording at fair value on the balance sheet and the offsetting of changes in fair value against interest expense. Additionally, it covers cross currency swaps, their transition from cash flow to fair value hedges, and the amortization of excluded components into interest expense. The section also mentions forward starting interest rate swaps used to hedge future cash flow variability related to forecasted debt issuances, with gains and losses recognized in other comprehensive income.

children.title: Cross Currency Swaps
children.summary: This section discusses cross currency swaps used to convert foreign currency cash flows into U.S. dollars and to stabilize cash payments in U.S. dollars. It details the transition from cash flow hedges to fair value hedges as of March 31, 2022, including the treatment of excluded components related to time value and cross currency basis spread. The section also explains how changes in the fair value of these swaps are recorded in financial statements, particularly in relation to interest expense and other comprehensive income. Additionally, it mentions the execution of additional cross currency swaps for Euro-denominated cash flows and their impact on financial reporting.

children.title: Forward Starting Interest Rate Swaps
children.summary: This section discusses forward starting interest rate swaps, which are used to manage exposure to interest rate changes on anticipated future transactions. These swaps are designated as cash flow hedges, allowing the company to hedge against variability in future cash flows related to forecasted debt issuances. Gains and losses from these swaps due to interest rate fluctuations are recorded in Other comprehensive income (loss). The section provides insight into the company's strategy for mitigating interest rate risk and the accounting treatment of these financial instruments.

children.title: Treasury Rate Locks
children.summary: This section discusses the company's use of treasury rate locks as cash flow hedges to manage interest rate risk, with gains and losses recorded in Other comprehensive income. It also details net investment hedges involving €750 million of Euro-denominated debt to mitigate foreign exchange exposure from non-U.S. subsidiaries. Additionally, it covers undesignated derivatives used as economic hedges, including foreign exchange forwards and swaptions, along with their notional values and recognized gains or losses. The section highlights credit risk concentrations related to financial instruments and the collateral arrangements in place with counterparties for derivative contracts.

children.title: Net Investment Hedges
children.summary: This section discusses net investment hedges, specifically the use of foreign currency debt instruments to mitigate foreign exchange exposure related to non-U.S. dollar investments in foreign subsidiaries. It details the notional amount of Euro-denominated debt designated as a net investment hedge, which was €750 million as of December 31 for both 2022 and 2021. Additionally, it covers treasury rate locks as cash flow hedges for interest rate risk and outlines undesignated derivatives used as economic hedges, including foreign exchange forwards and swaptions, along with their respective notional values and recognized gains or losses.

children.title: Undesignated Derivatives
children.summary: The section on Undesignated Derivatives covers the company's strategies for managing foreign exchange and interest rate risks through the use of foreign exchange forwards and swaptions. It details the notional values and pre-tax gains or losses associated with these derivatives for the years 2021 and 2022. The section also discusses the company's credit risk management practices, including collateral arrangements with counterparties, and its approach to treasury rate locks and net investment hedges to further mitigate financial risks.

children.title: Foreign Exchange Forwards
children.summary: This section discusses the use of foreign exchange forwards to manage foreign exchange rate risk associated with non-functional currency monetary assets and liabilities of international subsidiaries, specifically in British Pound Sterling and Euro. It details the notional values of foreign exchange forwards entered into and settled in the years 2022 and 2021, along with the pre-tax losses recognized in other income. Additionally, it mentions the use of swaptions for managing debt interest rates and outlines the company's approach to credit risk related to financial instruments and derivative contracts, including collateral arrangements with counterparties.

children.title: Swaptions
children.summary: This section discusses the use of swaptions as part of the company's strategy to manage interest rate risk by achieving a targeted mix of fixed and variable rate debt. It details the notional values of swaptions sold and settled, along with the pre-tax gains and losses recognized in interest expense. Additionally, the section outlines the company's approach to treasury rate locks and net investment hedges to mitigate interest rate and foreign exchange risks, respectively. It also highlights the company's credit risk management related to derivative contracts and the collateral arrangements in place with counterparties.

children.title: Concentrations of Credit Risk
children.summary: This section discusses concentrations of credit risk related to various financial instruments, including cash investments, trade receivables, and derivative contracts. It highlights the use of ISDA master agreements and credit support annex (CSA) agreements with major financial institutions to manage counterparty risk. The section details collateral arrangements, noting that as of December 31, 2022, $2.3 billion of collateral was posted for derivative contracts. It also assesses the risk of credit losses from counterparty nonperformance as remote, due to a diversified counterparty pool.

children.title: Note 10. Stock-Based Compensation
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's Long-Term Incentive Plan, focusing on the financial aspects of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Performance Stock Units (PSUs) granted under the 2017 Plan. It outlines the vesting schedules, classification of awards, and performance criteria for PSUs, which vest after three years based on specific goals. The section provides detailed data on RSU and PSU activity from 2020 to 2022, including outstanding shares, grants, payments, cancellations, and compensation expenses. It also reports stock-based compensation expenses totaling $609 million in 2022, highlighting the financial impact of Verizon's employee incentive programs.

children.title: Verizon Long-Term Incentive Plan
children.summary: The Verizon Long-Term Incentive Plan section outlines the structure and financial implications of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Performance Stock Units (PSUs) granted under the 2017 Plan. It details the vesting schedules, classification of awards as equity or liability, and performance criteria for PSUs, which vest after three years based on specific goals. The section includes comprehensive data on RSU and PSU activity from 2020 to 2022, including outstanding shares, grants, payments, cancellations, and associated compensation expenses. Additionally, it reports on stock-based compensation expenses, totaling $609 million in 2022, providing insights into Verizon's employee incentive programs and their financial impact.

children.title: Restricted Stock Units
children.summary: This section details the Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Performance Stock Units (PSUs) granted under Verizon's 2017 Plan. RSUs typically vest in three equal installments annually and can be classified as either equity or liability awards based on their settlement method. The section explains the treatment of dividend equivalent units (DEUs) and the estimation of forfeitures for RSUs. It also outlines the performance criteria for PSUs, which vest after three years based on achieved goals. Additionally, it provides a summary of RSU and PSU activity, including outstanding shares, grants, payments, and cancellations from 2020 to 2022, along with associated compensation expenses.

children.title: Performance Stock Units
children.summary: This section details the Performance Stock Units (PSUs) granted under Verizon's 2017 Plan, which vest at the end of a three-year performance cycle. The number of PSUs earned is determined by the Human Resources Committee based on performance goals. PSUs can be classified as either equity awards, measured at grant date fair value, or liability awards, measured at fair value at each reporting period. The section also includes data on RSU and PSU activity, unrecognized compensation expenses, and stock-based compensation expenses for the years 2020 to 2022.

children.title: Stock-Based Compensation Expense
children.summary: This section details Verizon's stock-based compensation expenses, specifically focusing on Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Performance Stock Units (PSUs) under the 2017 Plan. It outlines the vesting schedules, classification of awards as equity or liability, and the measurement of fair value for these awards. The section also provides statistics on the outstanding RSUs and PSUs, including grant, payment, and cancellation activity from 2020 to 2022. Additionally, it reports the after-tax compensation expenses related to stock-based compensation for the years 2020 to 2022, totaling $609 million in 2022. Readers can learn about the financial implications of stock-based compensation and the structure of Verizon's employee incentive programs.

children.title: Note 11. Employee Benefits
children.summary: This section details Verizon's employee benefits, including pension and postretirement obligations, funded status, and financial implications. It covers net actuarial gains, plan amendments from collective bargaining, and net periodic benefit costs, highlighting significant liabilities and contributions. Future benefit payments are estimated for pension and health care from 2023 to 2032, alongside discussions on employee stock ownership plans and severance benefits. The section emphasizes the financial impact of these benefits on the company's balance sheet and future obligations.

children.title: Pension and Other Postretirement Benefits
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's obligations and funded status related to employee benefits, focusing on defined benefit pension plans and postretirement health care and life insurance plans. It summarizes changes in benefit obligations and plan assets for the years ending December 31, 2022, and 2021, detailing service costs, interest costs, actuarial gains, and benefits paid. The section reports the funded status at year-end, indicating significant liabilities for both pension and health care plans, and outlines amounts recognized in the balance sheets and accumulated other comprehensive loss, emphasizing the financial implications of these benefits.

children.title: Obligations and Funded Status
children.summary: This section details the obligations and funded status of Verizon's employee benefits, specifically focusing on defined benefit pension plans and postretirement health care and life insurance plans. It provides a summary of changes in benefit obligations and plan assets for the years ending December 31, 2022, and 2021, including service costs, interest costs, actuarial gains, and benefits paid. The funded status at year-end is reported, showing significant liabilities for both pension and health care plans. Additionally, it outlines amounts recognized in the balance sheets and accumulated other comprehensive loss, highlighting the financial implications of these employee benefits.

children.title: Actuarial Gain, Net
children.summary: The section discusses the net actuarial gain for 2022, which amounts to $7.0 billion, attributed to an increase in the discount rate assumption for pension and postretirement benefit plans. It details the gains from previous years, highlighting a $1.1 billion gain in 2021. Additionally, it covers plan amendments resulting from collective bargaining agreements, which increased pension plan obligations by approximately $427 million. The section also provides financial data on accumulated and projected benefit obligations, as well as a summary of net periodic benefit costs for pension and postretirement plans over the years 2020 to 2022.

children.title: Plan Amendments
children.summary: This section discusses amendments to pension plans resulting from collective bargaining agreements ratified in July 2022, extending contracts with union members until August 2026. The amendments increased defined benefit pension plan obligations by approximately $427 million, impacting accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) by a net decrease of $317 million after taxes. It also details the financial implications of prior plan amendments from 2016 to 2018, which contributed to a net increase in pre-tax income. Additionally, it provides data on accumulated and projected benefit obligations for pension plans, highlighting the fair value of plan assets and net periodic benefit costs for pension and postretirement plans over the years 2020 to 2022.

children.title: Net Periodic Benefit Cost (Income)
children.summary: This section details the net periodic benefit cost related to pension and health care obligations, focusing on the weighted-average assumptions as of December 31 for 2022 and 2021. It specifies a discount rate of 5.20% for both types of obligations and a consistent compensation increase rate of 3.00%. Additionally, it discusses the discount rates for service and interest costs, expected returns on plan assets, and health care cost trend rates. The investment strategy for plan assets is also outlined, emphasizing a balanced asset allocation to meet benefit payments while managing associated risks.

children.title: Assumptions
children.summary: This section outlines the weighted-average assumptions used to determine pension and health care benefit obligations as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. Key assumptions include a discount rate of 5.20% for both pension and health care obligations in 2022, and a consistent rate of compensation increase at 3.00%. It details the discount rates for service and interest costs, expected returns on plan assets, and health care cost trend rates. The investment strategy for plan assets aims for a balanced mix to meet benefit payments while managing risk, with specific allocations to various asset classes and a focus on liability hedging.

children.title: Plan Assets
children.summary: The 'Plan Assets' section details the fair values of pension and other postretirement benefit plan assets as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. It includes specific dollar amounts and classifications of pension plan assets by type, such as cash, equity securities, and fixed income, categorized into Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 assets. The section also provides a reconciliation of pension plan assets, highlighting changes due to gains, losses, and transactions. For health care and life plans, it presents total fair values, asset breakdowns, and valuation methodologies, emphasizing the uncertainties in asset valuation and potential discrepancies in estimated fair values.

children.title: Pension Plans
children.summary: This section provides detailed fair values of pension plan assets categorized by asset type as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. It includes specific dollar amounts for cash and cash equivalents, equity securities, fixed income securities, real estate, private equity, and hedge funds, along with their classifications into Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 assets. Additionally, it outlines the reconciliation of pension plan assets measured at fair value, detailing changes in balances due to actual gains or losses, purchases, sales, and transfers. Readers can learn about the composition and valuation of pension plan investments over the specified years.

children.title: Health Care and Life Plans
children.summary: This section provides detailed fair value information for other postretirement benefit plans as of December 31, 2022, and 2021, categorized by asset type, including cash equivalents, equity securities, and fixed income securities. It outlines the total fair value of investments, which was $450 million in 2022 and $581 million in 2021, along with the breakdown of these values into Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 assets. The section also describes the valuation methodologies used for different asset categories, such as market prices for traded securities and NAV for commingled funds. Additionally, it highlights the inherent uncertainties in asset valuation and the potential for significant differences in estimated fair values.

children.title: Employer Contributions
children.summary: In 2022, the company made no discretionary contributions to qualified pension plans, contributed $53 million to nonqualified pension plans, and $692 million to other postretirement benefit plans. For 2023, discretionary contributions to qualified pension plans are expected to be around $200 million, with significant contributions to other postretirement benefit plans estimated at $820 million. The section also outlines future benefit payments to retirees, detailing expected pension and healthcare costs from 2023 to 2032. Additionally, it discusses the company's employee stock ownership plans, severance benefits, and recorded pension and benefits credits and charges for 2021 and 2022, highlighting significant actuarial adjustments and their financial impacts.

children.title: Estimated Future Benefit Payments
children.summary: This section outlines the estimated future benefit payments for pension and health care benefits to retirees from 2023 to 2032, detailing annual expected payments in millions of dollars. It specifies that pension benefits will total approximately $1.679 billion in 2023, decreasing slightly each year, with a total of $4.628 billion expected from 2028 to 2032. Health care and life benefits are also projected, starting at $867 million in 2023 and totaling $4.082 billion over the same five-year period. Additionally, it provides context on employer contributions to pension plans and the structure of employee stock ownership plans (ESOP).

children.title: Savings Plan and Employee Stock Ownership Plans
children.summary: This section discusses the company's employee stock ownership plans (ESOP) and savings plans, highlighting that four leveraged ESOPs are maintained, with 43 million allocated shares as of December 31, 2022. The company matches a percentage of eligible employee contributions to savings plans with shares from the ESOP. It also provides a financial overview of total savings plan costs, which were $620 million in 2022, down from $730 million in 2020. Additionally, it outlines the absence of unallocated shares in the ESOP and notes that all leveraged ESOP shares are included in earnings per share calculations.

children.title: Severance Benefits
children.summary: The Severance Benefits section outlines the financial implications of severance, pension, and benefits charges for the company. It reports a net pre-tax pension and benefits credit of $1.7 billion in 2022, driven by an increase in the discount rate for pension liabilities, and details expected employer contributions to pension plans in 2023. The section also provides estimated future benefit payments to retirees and a breakdown of severance liabilities, noting a net pre-tax severance charge of $319 million in 2022. Additionally, it discusses the costs associated with employee stock ownership plans.

children.title: Severance, Pension and Benefits (Credits) Charges
children.summary: This section details the financial aspects of severance, pension, and benefits charges for the company. In 2022, the company recorded net pre-tax pension and benefits credits of $1.7 billion, primarily due to an increase in the discount rate assumption for pension liabilities. It also outlines employer contributions to pension plans, with significant expected contributions in 2023. The section includes estimated future benefit payments to retirees and provides a breakdown of severance liabilities over the years, highlighting a net pre-tax severance charge of $319 million in 2022. Additionally, it discusses the company's employee stock ownership plans and associated costs.

children.title: Note 12. Taxes
children.summary: This section covers the company's tax-related financial information, focusing on deferred tax assets and liabilities, as well as unrecognized tax benefits. It details deferred tax assets totaling $11.467 billion and liabilities of $54.735 billion, resulting in a net deferred tax liability of $43.268 billion as of December 31, 2022. The section also mentions $2.5 billion in undistributed foreign earnings exempt from U.S. deferred taxes. Additionally, it provides a reconciliation of unrecognized tax benefits, which amounted to $2.812 billion, with potential impacts on the effective income tax rate. The section further discusses net after-tax expenses related to interest and penalties from 2020 to 2022.

children.title: Deferred Tax Assets and Liabilities
children.summary: This section discusses deferred tax assets and liabilities, highlighting the differences between book and tax bases of assets and liabilities. Key components include deferred tax assets related to employee benefits, tax loss carryforwards, and other assets, totaling $11.467 billion as of December 31, 2022. Deferred tax liabilities, primarily from intangible amortization and depreciation, amount to $54.735 billion, resulting in a net deferred tax liability of $43.268 billion. The section also addresses undistributed foreign earnings of $2.5 billion, which are not subject to U.S. deferred taxes due to their indefinite reinvestment outside the U.S. Additionally, it outlines unrecognized tax benefits and their potential impact on the effective income tax rate.

children.title: Unrecognized Tax Benefits
children.summary: This section discusses unrecognized tax benefits, detailing the reconciliation of their balances from 2020 to 2022. It highlights the beginning and ending balances, additions based on current and prior year tax positions, reductions, settlements, and lapses of statutes of limitations. As of December 31, 2022, the balance of unrecognized tax benefits was $2.812 billion, with $2.5 billion of this amount potentially favorably impacting the effective income tax rate if recognized. Additionally, it notes the net after-tax expenses related to interest and penalties for the years 2020 to 2022.

children.title: Note 13. Segment Information
children.summary: This section provides an overview of Verizon's two reportable segments: Consumer and Business, detailing their activities and financial performance, including operating revenues and income for 2022 and 2021. It highlights the Consumer segment's focus on wireless and wireline services, while the Business segment encompasses data, video, and corporate networking solutions. Additionally, it includes a reconciliation of operating revenues and expenses from these segments to the consolidated financial information for 2020, 2021, and 2022, detailing external revenues, costs, and adjustments for eliminations. This information is crucial for stakeholders to understand the operational structure and financial health of Verizon's business units, as well as the impact of special items on segment performance.

children.title: Reportable Segments
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's two reportable segments: Consumer and Business, detailing their principal activities and financial performance. The Consumer segment focuses on wireless and wireline communications services, while the Business segment offers a range of services including data, video, and corporate networking solutions. Financial data for 2022 and 2021 is provided, showing operating revenues, costs, and operating income for each segment. The report also highlights the impact of the sale of Verizon Media and includes information on intersegment revenues and other revenue sources. Overall, this section serves to inform stakeholders about the operational structure and financial health of Verizon's business units.

children.title: Reconciliation to Consolidated Financial Information
children.summary: This section provides a detailed reconciliation of operating revenues and expenses from reportable segments to consolidated financial information for the years ended December 31, 2020, 2021, and 2022. It includes specific figures for external operating revenues, costs associated with services and wireless equipment, and total operating expenses for both Consumer and Business segments. The reconciliation highlights the total reportable segment revenues, corporate and other revenues, and adjustments for eliminations, culminating in the consolidated operating revenues. Readers can learn about the financial performance of different segments and how special items affect overall assessments of segment performance.

children.title: Note 14. Equity and Comprehensive Income (Loss)
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's equity activities from 2020 to 2022, including common stock transactions, noncontrolling interests, and a reconciliation of operating income to consolidated income before taxes. It highlights the absence of share repurchases, the issuance of common stock for employee plans, and the acquisition of TracFone, along with additional interests in wireless partnerships. The section also details the components of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss), such as foreign currency adjustments and unrealized gains/losses, providing a reconciliation of these components and their impact on comprehensive income. Overall, it outlines the financial implications of equity transactions and comprehensive income changes on Verizon's overall equity position.

children.title: Equity
children.summary: The Equity section details Verizon's financial activities related to common stock and noncontrolling interests from 2020 to 2022. It includes a reconciliation of operating income to consolidated income before taxes, highlighting corporate expenses, severance charges, and pension costs. The section notes that no shares were repurchased during this period and discusses the issuance of common stock for employee plans and the acquisition of TracFone. Additionally, it covers Verizon's acquisition of additional interests in wireless partnerships, the financial implications of these equity transactions, and their effects on additional paid-in capital and noncontrolling interest.

children.title: Common Stock
children.summary: This section provides a reconciliation of operating income from reportable segments to consolidated income before taxes for the years 2020-2022. It details the operating income figures, corporate expenses, severance charges, pension costs, and other financial components affecting the overall income. The section also discusses the company's share buyback program, noting that no shares were repurchased during the specified years, and outlines the issuance of common stock for employee plans and the acquisition of TracFone. Additionally, it covers transactions related to noncontrolling interests and the components of accumulated other comprehensive income.

children.title: Noncontrolling Interests
children.summary: This section discusses Verizon's acquisition of additional interests in controlled wireless partnerships, totaling $508 million in cash for the year ended December 31, 2022. It explains that these transactions were treated as equity transactions since Verizon maintains a controlling financial interest, leading to a $450 million reduction in additional paid-in capital and a $58 million reduction in noncontrolling interest. The financial impacts of these transactions are reflected in the consolidated statement of changes in equity and cash flows for the year.

children.title: Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss)
children.summary: This section details the components of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss) for Verizon, which includes foreign currency translation adjustments, unrealized gains and losses on cash flow and fair value hedges, marketable securities, and defined benefit pension plans. It provides a reconciliation of these components from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2022, highlighting significant changes and the net impact on comprehensive income. The amounts are presented net of taxes and include reclassifications to net income, which are reflected in the consolidated statements of income. Readers can learn about the financial implications of these components on Verizon's overall equity and the specific factors contributing to changes in comprehensive income over the years.

children.title: Note 15. Additional Financial Information
children.summary: Note 15 provides comprehensive financial information for Verizon, including detailed income statement metrics from 2020 to 2022, such as depreciation, interest costs, and advertising expenses, which inform assessments of financial health. It also includes balance sheet data for 2021 and 2022, highlighting prepaid expenses, accounts payable, and accrued liabilities, crucial for understanding liquidity. Additionally, cash flow information from 2020 to 2022 details interest payments, net cash flows, and significant operational impacts, alongside commitments and contingencies related to litigation and regulatory matters, including unconditional purchase obligations totaling $24.5 billion.

children.title: Income Statement Information
children.summary: This section provides detailed income statement information for the years ended December 31 from 2020 to 2022, including key financial metrics such as depreciation expense, interest costs on debt, capitalized interest costs, and advertising expenses. It also outlines other income and expenses, including interest income and net debt extinguishment losses. Readers can learn about the trends in these financial figures over the three years, which can inform assessments of the company's financial health and operational efficiency.

children.title: Balance Sheet Information
children.summary: This section provides detailed balance sheet information for Verizon as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021, including prepaid expenses, accounts payable, and accrued liabilities. Key figures include prepaid taxes, deferred contract costs, and collateral payments related to derivative contracts. It also outlines accounts payable totaling $8.75 billion in 2022 and accrued expenses of $7.82 billion. Additionally, it highlights property, plant, and equipment additions that remain unpaid, amounting to approximately $6.0 billion in 2022. This information is crucial for understanding Verizon's financial position and liquidity.

children.title: Cash Flow Information
children.summary: This section provides detailed cash flow information for Verizon over the years 2020 to 2022, including cash paid for interest and income taxes, as well as net cash flows from operating and financing activities. Key figures include interest payments decreasing from $4,420 million in 2020 to $3,316 million in 2022, and significant changes in device payment plan receivables. The section also outlines net debt extinguishment losses and gains from business dispositions, highlighting the financial impacts of various operational decisions. Additionally, it discusses Verizon's commitments and contingencies related to litigation and regulatory proceedings, as well as unconditional purchase obligations totaling $24.5 billion, primarily for network equipment and services.

children.title: Note 16. Commitments and Contingencies
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's commitments and contingencies related to ongoing litigation and regulatory proceedings. It details the company's approach to establishing accruals for probable and estimable losses, noting that currently pending matters are not material. Verizon is involved in approximately 25 patent infringement cases, primarily from non-practicing entities, with some potentially going to trial. The section also discusses Verizon's renewable energy purchase agreements (REPAs) and unconditional purchase obligations totaling $24.5 billion, primarily for network equipment and services, with specific amounts allocated to future years.

children.summary: This section states that there are no changes or disagreements with accountants regarding accounting and financial disclosure. children.title: Item 9A. Controls and Procedures
children.summary: This section covers Verizon's evaluation of its disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2022, confirming their effectiveness and absence of material weaknesses, supported by an attestation from Ernst & Young LLP. It details the ongoing implementation of a new global enterprise resource planning (ERP) system aimed at enhancing financial reporting processes, data analysis, and reporting speed. The section emphasizes management's responsibility for internal controls and the criteria used for evaluation, noting that while changes may occur during ERP implementation, no material changes affecting internal controls were identified in the fourth quarter of 2022.

children.title: Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures
children.summary: This section discusses the evaluation of Verizon's disclosure controls and procedures as mandated by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer assessed the effectiveness of these controls as of December 31, 2022, concluding they were effective. It also outlines the ongoing implementation of a new global enterprise resource planning (ERP) system aimed at improving financial reporting processes. Additionally, it confirms that there were no material weaknesses identified in internal controls over financial reporting, supported by an attestation report from Ernst & Young LLP.

children.title: Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting
children.summary: This section discusses the ongoing review and enhancement of Verizon's internal control over financial reporting, particularly in light of a multi-year implementation of a new global enterprise resource planning (ERP) system initiated in 2020. The new ERP system aims to improve financial information flow, data analysis, and reporting speed. It notes that while changes to processes and procedures may occur during implementation, no material changes affecting internal controls were identified in the fourth quarter of 2022. Management has assessed the effectiveness of internal controls as of December 31, 2022, concluding that they are effective and free of material weaknesses, with an attestation report from Ernst & Young LLP included in the report.

children.title: Management's Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting
children.summary: This section outlines Verizon's management responsibility for internal control over financial reporting, emphasizing the evaluation conducted using the criteria from the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. As of December 31, 2022, management assessed the internal controls as effective, with no material weaknesses identified. Additionally, the independent accounting firm Ernst & Young LLP has provided an attestation report on these controls, reinforcing the assessment's credibility. The section also notes ongoing changes due to the implementation of a new global ERP system, which may affect internal controls in the future.

children.title: Item 9B. Other Information

children.summary: This section provides details about Verizon's current executive officers, including their names, ages, and positions held since specific years.
